description: Erection of a single storey side and rear extension, formation of a front entrance porch and provision of a raised rear deck area with steps and balustrade.
decision_conditions: The proposed front porch, by reason of its sitting on higher ground and excessive width, height, choice of gable-end roof design and contemporary fenestration and entrance door, would appear overly prominent on this elevation and would visually compete with the characteristic gable-end bay features and ground floor roof on the front elevation of the house that contribute to the unique design of the dwellings in this part of Hawthorn Road streetscene. Moreover, the proposed porch extension would unbalance the pair of semi-detached dwellings, disrupting the established visual symmetry between the two, causing significant and unacceptable harm to the character and appearance of the dwelling, the pair of semi-detached dwellings and this section of Hawthorn Road where gable-end roofed porches with contemporary fenestration and detailing are not a common feature. As such, the proposal would result in significant harm to the host property, Hawthorn Road streetscene and the Park Hill Road Area of Special Local Character, contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and the guidance in Supplementary Planning Document 4 "Design of Residential Extensions" (SPD 4) and SPD 14 "Creating Locally Distinctive Places" and Park Hill Road ASLC - Character Appraisal (2020).

The proposed single storey side/rear extension, by reason of its excessive depth and eaves height and close proximity to the western boundary, the rear primary windows and rear amenity area of No. 16A,B,C Hawthorn Road, would create an un-neighbourly sense of enclosure and loss of outlook from the rear garden and rear windows of ground floor and first floor flats at Nos. 16A,B,C, causing an adverse amenity impact to the occupants of these adjacent flats. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policy 29 of Sutton's Local Plan 2018.

The proposed raised patio along the eastern boundary with No. 14 Hawthorn Road, due to lack of any mitigation measures by way of a timber fence or screening, would result in an adverse amenity impact to the occupants of this property in terms of loss of privacy to their rear garden. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policy 29 of the Local Plan 2018.
